# Branch Dispositions — the repository fact

**Created by phase GOV-3 on 2026-09-04** (branch `agrimore/gov3-agrimore-skill-and-branch-model`,
from `main` = `c8f6f30`). This file exists because, until today, every decision about what should
happen to a branch in this repository lived only in one CTO session's private memory, and sessions
do not share memory. Four or more concurrent sessions have edited this checkout at once
(`agrimore-concurrency-incidents` in CTO memory: seven incidents, one materially false commit
message), always colliding on `firestore.rules` and `functions/src/index.ts`. A row here is the
only way a second session can discover that a phase is already claimed.

**This file is the authority on branch disposition. Session memory is not.** Operating rules:
`.claude/skills/agrimore/references/{merge,promote}.md`; validator:
`node scripts/governance/validate-branch-dispositions.mjs` (warnings only, exit 0 — read them).

## The rules

- **A branch absent from this file has NO disposition and MUST NOT be merged.** Absence is not
  neutral. Find out before merging.
- **Only the owner changes a disposition.** A session may ADD a row for a branch it just created
  and may move its OWN row `ACTIVE` → `MERGED_DEVELOP` in the bookkeeping commit after the merge.
  A session never changes another branch's `Status` cell — not even to correct it. Flag and ask.
- **CLAIM BEFORE YOU START — the row is a lock, not a receipt.** See the claim protocol.
- **Phase branches merge into `develop`, never into `main`.** `develop` is the integration branch
  (local end-to-end on the Firebase emulator suite). `staging` and `main` move only by
  fast-forward promotion with the owner's word in the same message, recorded in `## Promotions`.
  A merge commit or a direct commit on `staging`/`main` is a defect.
- **Nothing here authorises `firebase deploy`.** Promotion is a git event. Deploying to
  `agrimore-66a4e` (live, real users) is the owner's own action, always with explicit function
  names; the skill prints the command and stops.

## Claim protocol — read this before creating a branch

1. **Collision check, three sources, every time:** `git worktree list` · `git branch --list
   'agrimore/*'` · this file's `ACTIVE` rows, read for topic overlap (not just branch name). A
   claim row on an unmerged branch is invisible from `develop` — that is why all three are needed.
2. **Create the worktree from `main`** (or from `develop` once phases have landed there — the
   contract's `base` says which): `git worktree add ../Agrimore-<slug> -b agrimore/<id>-<slug> <base>`.
3. **The claim row is the FIRST commit on the branch.** `Status` = `ACTIVE`, `Why` names the files
   you expect to touch and the collision check you ran, `Merged into` = `N/A — pending`.
   Commit message: `docs(repo): claim phase <ID> — <slug>`. Verify with
   `git log -1 --format='%an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>'` (must be `Agrimore <agrimorein@gmail.com>`).
4. Keep the `Why` cell growing with findings; commit ledger edits immediately.
5. After the merge (inside the `develop` worktree): the bookkeeping commit sets your row to
   `MERGED_DEVELOP`, fills `SHA` with the branch tip and `Merged into` with the merge commit.

## Status tokens

| Token | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ENVIRONMENT` | One of `develop` · `staging` · `main`. Moves only per the fast-forward model; its `SHA` cell is informational (re-measure), never a lock. |
| `ACTIVE` | In flight, owned by a running phase. No disposition decided yet — expected. |
| `MERGED_DEVELOP` | Contained in `develop`. `Merged into` names the `--no-ff` merge commit on `develop`. Reaches `staging`/`main` only through a promotion recorded below. |
| `MERGED` | Legacy: contained in `main` from before the branch model existed (the tip sits on `main`'s own history). |
| `PRESERVED_REFERENCE` | Deliberately **NOT** merged; kept as input to a named future phase. **NEVER merge without a new owner decision.** |
| `SUPERSEDED_BY:<branch>` | Replaced by `<branch>`. Do not merge this branch. |
| `ARCHIVED_TAG:<tag>` | Content preserved as tag `<tag>`; the branch may be deleted. |

The REAL, currently-live gap is a TIMING one: `FCMService().initialize()` — the only thing that calls `_saveTokenToFirestore()` — runs exactly ONCE, in `main.dart`, at app cold-start, and only persists a token if `FirebaseAuth.instance.currentUser` is ALREADY non-null at that exact moment. A returning customer who was already signed in before relaunching gets their token saved correctly on relaunch. A customer's FIRST sign-in in a given app session — the common case for a fresh install, or signing in after a logout without restarting the app — does NOT, because `initialize()` already ran (with no user) before the login screen even rendered, and nothing calls it or an equivalent save again afterward anywhere in `apps/marketplace`. `apps/delivery` and `apps/employee` do not have this gap because THEIR OWN `auth_provider.dart` files call a private `_updateFCMToken(uid)` helper explicitly, right after every successful sign-in, independent of `FCMService`'s app-startup timing — confirmed by reading `apps/delivery/lib/providers/auth_provider.dart:62,100,114-131`. `apps/admin` and `apps/seller` have the SAME gap marketplace does (neither has an equivalent per-login save either) but are out of this phase's scope, unchanged from the original contract, because `sendBroadcastNotification`'s intended audience is customers. SEPARATELY, and NOT a schema question at all: `sendBroadcastNotification` (`functions/src/admin/notifications.ts:354`) builds its audience with its OWN inline `doc.data().fcmTokens || []` — reading ONLY the array field, not the file's own shared `uniqueTokens()` helper (`:35-50`) that `sendNotificationToUser`/`sendOrderUpdateNotification` already use, which ALSO checks the singular `fcmToken` as a fallback. This means even a user whose token exists ONLY as the singular field (a stale document from before `fcm_service.dart` started writing both, or a hypothetical future regression) is silently excluded from every broadcast, though currently reached by the two single-recipient functions. **N-17, re-verified unchanged**: `notifications.ts:348` (`admin.firestore().collection("users").get()`) loads the entire collection with no pagination inside a 256MiB callable. In scope: WS1 add an explicit post-login FCM token save to `apps/marketplace/lib/providers/auth_provider.dart`, mirroring `apps/delivery`'s own `_updateFCMToken(uid)` pattern, called from every genuine new-session success path (`registerWithEmail`, `signInWithEmail`, `verifyPhoneOTP`, `signInWithGoogle` — identified by their `_logAuthEvent(..., true, ...)` markers, not by line-number guessing); WS2 make `sendBroadcastNotification` reuse the existing `uniqueTokens()` helper instead of its own array-only inline read; WS3 paginate the user scan. | `agrimore/fix16-createorder-bounds` | `f081ec8` | `MERGED_DEVELOP` | 2026-09-05 | session FIX-16 | Phase FIX-16: bound how fast and how large an authenticated caller can create orders (finding **N-23**). RE-VERIFIED at base `c85258f` (develop tip after the FIX-15 merge), not carried from the contract's `2f5252c` text: read `createOrder.ts` directly — no per-user rate limit exists anywhere in the function, and a COD order costs the caller nothing to create, so an authenticated script can call it without bound; `deliveryAddress`/`notes`/`deliverySlot`/`orderType`/`autoFrequency` are all written into the order document verbatim from client input (`:650-653`) with no shape or size check anywhere before that write. **WS1** (rate limit): FIRST ATTEMPT was a flat per-uid cooldown mirroring `createAssociateOnboardingPayment.ts`'s `onboarding_rate_limits` pattern (`ORDER_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = 10_000`, one order per 10s) — REVERTED after the full `gate.sh --full --emulator` battery (68 suites) caught it regressing FOUR existing suites with `failed=4`: `phase14_payment_replay_test`, `phase15_order_integrity_test`, `phase27_stock_integrity_test`, `phaseD_redemption_test` — all of which legitimately call `createOrder` a second time for the SAME uid within seconds (retrying with a different coupon, attempting a double spend that must be rejected for ITS OWN reason, a second real order after stock moved). This is real evidence, not a test-fixture inconvenience: a genuine customer does the same thing (places one order, then immediately places a separate one for something they forgot), so a flat cooldown between ANY two calls was the wrong shape of control. REPLACED with a fixed-window COUNTER: `order_rate_limits/{uid}` now stores `{windowStart, count}`, allowing up to `MAX_ORDERS_PER_WINDOW = 8` successful orders per `ORDER_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = 60_000` (60s), still read/written INSIDE `createOrder`'s own existing transaction so the check-then-write stays atomic with the order-creation writes it gates. 8/60s is a generous engineering safety margin, not a measured business ceiling (same class of judgment call as FIX-12's `MAX_SENDS_PER_IP_PER_DAY = 50`) — comfortably above every same-uid call pattern in this codebase's own suites (none exceeds 2), while still turning "unlimited" into a real, enforced ceiling (≤480/hour) against a burst-abuse script. Marked only after every other write for the order has been queued, so a caller who fails validation or hits a precondition later in the same transaction never consumes a window slot for an order that didn't happen. Re-ran all four regressed suites directly after the fix — all pass with their correct rejection reasons, not the rate limiter's. **WS2** (input bounds): `MAX_DELIVERY_ADDRESS_BYTES = 4096` (measured against `AddressModel.toMap()`'s real fields — name/phone/two address lines/city/state/zipcode/country/landmark/lat-lng — which serialize to well under 1 KB), `MAX_NOTES_LENGTH = 500`, `MAX_SHORT_STRING_FIELD_LENGTH = 100` for `deliverySlot`/`orderType`/`autoFrequency`; `deliveryAddress` additionally checked to be a non-array object. Runs before any Firestore read (pure input validation), so an oversized payload fails fast with a clean `invalid-argument` instead of riding through the whole transaction only to hit Firestore's 1 MiB document-size limit at commit time. **WS3**: `functions/scripts/phase36_createorder_bounds_test.js`, 10 scenarios covering both the rate-limit counter (8 back-to-back distinct orders from one uid all succeed, a 9th in the same window is refused and creates no order, a different uid is unaffected, the window resets after it expires) and each input-bounds check (oversized/malformed `deliveryAddress`, oversized `notes`/`deliverySlot`/`autoFrequency`, plus a positive control with real-shape values). `must_not_touch`: `storage.rules`, `apps/**`, `packages/**` (out of scope — WS1/WS2 are entirely server-side). Rather than extend `createOrder.ts` with a new client-triggerable custom-price path in the same phase that also builds the negotiation UI, **this phase is deliberately narrowed to the negotiation mechanism only** — a buyer and seller reach a locked, mutually-accepted price/quantity — and does NOT yet wire an accepted RFQ into `createOrder.ts`. That integration (the actual money-moving step) is split to a new phase RFQ-3, sized and reviewed on its own once this mechanism is proven. Objective: new `rfqs/{rfqId}` collection + three callables (v2 `onCall`, mirroring `createOrder.ts`'s server-derived-everything discipline for whatever it DOES touch): `createRfq({productId, quantity, proposedPrice?, notes?})` (buyer-initiated; validates the product exists and `isB2BEnabled === true` — mirrors `orderPricing.ts:269`'s exact check; resolves `sellerId` from `products/{productId}.sellerId` server-side, never client-supplied; creates the doc `status:'pending'`, `awaitingResponseFrom:'seller'`, appends an append-only `history` entry — mirrors the Product Credit ledger's append-only philosophy over in-place mutation, so a negotiation's full back-and-forth is always reconstructable), `submitRfqOffer({rfqId, price, quantity, notes})` (either party may submit a new offer ONLY when `awaitingResponseFrom` names their own role — derived server-side from whether `request.auth.uid` matches the rfq's `buyerId` or `sellerId`, never a client-asserted role; flips `awaitingResponseFrom` to the other party; appends history), `respondToRfqOffer({rfqId, action:'accept'|'reject'})` (accept locks `finalPrice`/`finalQuantity`/`acceptedAt` from the last offer and sets `status:'accepted'`; reject sets `status:'rejected'`; only the party currently awaited may call this). Rules: `rfqs/{rfqId}` — `allow read: if isOwner(resource.data.buyerId) || isOwner(resource.data.sellerId) || isAdmin()`; `allow write: if false` (CF-only, mirrors `orders/{orderId}`'s `allow create: if false` shape exactly). No client UI this phase (RFQ-2's job) — proven entirely through emulator callable + rules suites, mirroring `phase37`/`phase37b`'s pairing. | `agrimore/fix-v1-trigger-fieldvalue` | `496f360` | `MERGED_DEVELOP` | 2026-09-07 | session P0-FIELDVALUE | **P0 — live money not paid.** Owner-directed (picked up the background task spawned during RFQ-3's security lane, `task_0ca9a0e7`, originally scoped to `orderNotifications.ts`'s crash alone; escalated after investigation revealed a systemic, live, money-impacting bug — the owner explicitly chose "fix everything now" when presented with the finding). ROOT CAUSE, established with direct evidence, not assumed: `admin.firestore.FieldValue`/`.Timestamp` (the legacy namespace-style static property access) is **undefined** specifically inside the isolated child process the Firebase Functions emulator spins up for a REAL, externally-triggered background function invocation (`runBackground`/`processBackground` in firebase-tools' own `functionsEmulatorRuntime.js`) — even though `admin.apps.length === 1` (the app IS initialized) and `require.resolve("firebase-admin")` resolves to the single correct module. Proven via a diagnostic instrumented copy of the COMPILED output (never committed, restored to a byte-identical fresh-`tsc` state immediately after): `Object.keys(admin.firestore)` is `[]` in that context; `require("firebase-admin/firestore").FieldValue` (the MODULAR export) is a real function in the SAME context; switching the crash site to the modular import resolved it completely, re-verified live. This does NOT affect v1/v2 `onCall` callables (client-invoked, a materially different dispatch path — `runFunction` without `runBackground`/`processBackground` in every callable's own stack trace, and this session's own extensive testing of `createOrder.ts`/`rfq.ts`/`payment.ts`/`wallet.ts`/etc. via `test.wrap()` has never once hit this) — confirmed additionally by REPRODUCING THE SAME CRASH via a genuine external Firestore `.update()` write (not `test.wrap()`, which runs in-process and gives FALSE CONFIDENCE — `phase16d1_commission_test.js`'s own "ALL PASSED" result is exactly this false positive) against `payEmployeeCommissionOnDelivery`: a real order transition to `delivered` left `wallet.balance` at `0` and `order.commissionPaid` at `false` — **Sales Associate commissions are not being paid on real, delivered orders in the live production system right now.** SCOPE DECISION (evidence-based, not "fix every file matching the string"): grepped the entire `functions/src` tree for `admin.firestore.(FieldValue|Timestamp|GeoPoint|FieldPath)` — 36 files match, but MOST of them (28) are used ONLY from `onCall` callables (including `createOrder.ts`, `payment.ts`, `wallet.ts`, `rfq.ts` — this codebase's own most security-sensitive, most extensively-proven-working files) and are NOT part of this bug's confirmed dispatch-mechanism class; touching them adds real regression risk to files this codebase has repeatedly, explicitly protected for zero benefit. Fixing ONLY the confirmed-at-risk set: files that themselves define a v1 Firestore trigger or v1/v2 background schedule AND use the pattern, PLUS one shared helper confirmed reached transitively from such a trigger's own call graph (`productCreditLedger.ts`, imported by `productCreditReversal.ts` — itself a `functions.firestore...onWrite` trigger with no DIRECT `FieldValue` reference of its own, so it never appeared in the raw grep, but genuinely at risk through `appendLedgerEntry`'s own use of the pattern; confirmed by reading the import graph, not assumed). Files to fix (9): `admin/notifications.ts` (`onOrderStatusChanged`, CONFIRMED crashed live), `customer/employeeCommission.ts` (`payEmployeeCommissionOnDelivery`, CONFIRMED crashed live, **the P0**), `customer/inventory.ts` (`onProductStockChanged`, CONFIRMED crashed live), `customer/orderNotifications.ts` (`onOrderCreatedNotifications`, CONFIRMED crashed live — the originally-scoped finding), `customer/sellerNotifications.ts` (`notifySellerNewOrder` + `calculateSellerPayout` — the latter is ALSO seller-payout money and was seen entering its real logic body in the same live repro run, at risk though not independently isolated), `customer/productCreditExpiry.ts` (`expireProductCredits`/`releaseExpiredProductCreditHolds`, v1 `functions.pubsub.schedule` — same background-dispatch class by architecture; this environment has no pubsub emulator configured (`firebase.json` declares no pubsub port, confirmed by the emulator's own "function ignored because the pubsub emulator does not exist" messages seen repeatedly this session), so these two cannot be independently reproduced the same way — fixed defensively on the strength of the confirmed pattern-match, disclosed as not independently reproduced), `customer/benefitAccrual.ts` (`accrueMonthlyBenefits`, same pubsub-schedule class, same reproduction limitation), `employee/adminOnboardingActions.ts` (`requestAssociateOnboardingRefundOnSuspend`, a `functionsV1.firestore...onUpdate` trigger — refund-request money-adjacent), `customer/productCreditLedger.ts` (shared helper, transitively at risk per above). Fix: replace every `admin.firestore.FieldValue`/`.Timestamp`/`.GeoPoint`/`.FieldPath` reference in these 9 files with the modular `import { FieldValue, Timestamp, ... } from "firebase-admin/firestore";` equivalent — behaviorally identical when the namespace access DOES work (proven: both produce the exact same sentinel/value), strictly safer when it doesn't. Files expected: `docs/active/BRANCH_DISPOSITIONS.md` (this row), the 9 files above. `may_write`: exactly those 10 paths. `must_not_touch`: the 27 callable-only files sharing the same string pattern (confirmed safe, explicitly left alone — see scope decision above), any RFQ-3 file (separate, unmerged, unrelated worktree). Lanes: security (money correctness, the core reason this phase exists). The contract's own note explicitly warned "do not trust this note's line-level assumptions" — re-derived the exact current shape of `createOrder.ts` (926 lines) and `orderPricing.ts` (453 lines) fresh, in full, rather than trusting the placeholder. MAJOR RE-SCOPE from the contract's original plan ("createOrder.ts accepts an optional rfqId..."): `computeOrderPricing` (the function BOTH `createOrder.ts` and `productCreditHold.ts`'s `quoteOrderWithCredit` call, specifically so the two can never disagree on a number — see that file's own header) has NO per-item price-override hook anywhere; every price is either `product.b2bPrice` or `product.salePrice`, selected by `orderMode` alone. Weaving "sometimes this one item uses a THIRD price, from an RFQ" into that shared function risks the exact kind of two-computations-must-agree drift `orderPricing.ts` was extracted specifically to prevent, and touches `createOrder.ts` itself — this codebase's single most security-sensitive, most collision-prone file (every historical concurrent-session incident touched it; SEC/FIX phases 1,3,4,9,16 all hardened it independently). DECIDED: build a NEW, separate callable (`createOrderFromRfq`, new file `functions/src/customer/createOrderFromRfq.ts`) rather than modifying `createOrder.ts`'s own transaction at all — **`createOrder.ts` and `orderPricing.ts` are NOT touched by this phase**, eliminating all regression risk to the general checkout path. The new callable: re-reads `rfqs/{rfqId}` server-side inside its own transaction (fresh, never trusted from the client beyond the id string); validates `status === 'accepted'`, `request.auth.uid === rfq.buyerId` (never a client-asserted role, mirroring `rfq.ts`'s own discipline), and — the double-spend guard — `!rfq.consumedByOrderId`, checked before any write, mirroring `verified_payments.consumedByOrderId`'s exact idempotency-anchor shape; validates the single submitted item's `productId`/`quantity` match `rfq.productId`/`rfq.finalQuantity` EXACTLY; prices the line at `rfq.finalPrice` (never re-derived, never client-supplied) x `rfq.finalQuantity`, with the SAME client-supplied-with-sanity-ceiling `deliveryCharge`/`tax` handling `orderPricing.ts` already uses (an unrelated, already-established "trust but cap" concern, not part of the negotiated price's own integrity); creates exactly ONE order document for `rfq.sellerId` (single product/single seller, no per-seller ratio split needed); forces `orderMode: 'B2B'` (matching `rfq.ts`'s own `isB2BEnabled === true` gate at RFQ-creation time) but explicitly EXEMPTS this path from the normal "B2B requires employeeCode" rule — an RFQ is a direct buyer-seller negotiation with no Sales Associate attribution point anywhere in RFQ-1/RFQ-2, so `employeeUid`/`employeeCode` are always `null` for an RFQ order, a deliberate, disclosed departure from `createOrder.ts`'s own B2B rule, not an oversight; reuses `order_rate_limits/{uid}` (the SAME counter `createOrder.ts` uses — a burst of RFQ-orders should be bounded by the same ceiling, not a separate one), the SAME profile-completeness check, the SAME stock-decrement pattern (one product, `productSnaps`/`productRefs` of length 1), and duplicates (not extracts) `createOrder.ts`'s own payment-verification block (HMAC/live-status already happened in `payment.ts`; this only re-checks the `verified_payments` document) — a deliberate, comment-linked duplication rather than a shared extraction, since unlike pricing, a single self-contained "does this payment cover this payable amount" check has no two-systems-must-agree hazard, and extracting it would require touching `createOrder.ts` to call the extraction, reintroducing exactly the regression surface this design avoids; marks `rfqs/{rfqId}.consumedByOrderId`/`consumedAt` inside the same transaction's write phase. Product Credit holds are explicitly NOT supported on an RFQ order (stacking a hold discount on an already-negotiated bespoke price is an unresolved product question the contract never asked for) — `productCreditHoldId` is simply not accepted by this callable's input shape. Once consumed, an RFQ stays consumed even if the resulting order is later cancelled — mirrors `verified_payments`' own behavior (a consumed payment is never "un-consumed" by a cancellation either; refund/reversal is a separate, manual, out-of-band concern nowhere in this codebase automates for payments, so RFQ consumption is held to the identical standard, not a stricter or looser one) — a deliberate, disclosed simplification, not a silent gap. RULES FINDING (revises the contract's own guess): `rfqs/{rfqId}` already has a BLANKET `allow write: if false` (confirmed by reading `firestore.rules:1393-1396` fresh) — adding `consumedByOrderId` to it needs NO rules change at all, since literally every field is already CF-only. The REAL rules change is elsewhere: `orders/{orderId}`'s three update-guard functions (`ownerCannotChangeOrderFinancials` `:345-349`, `orderFulfilmentCannotChangeProtectedFields` `:428-436`, `deliveryPartnerCanClaimOrder` `:450-457`) are explicit HARDCODED FIELD-NAME denylists, not a blanket-deny-unlisted-fields mechanism (confirmed by reading all three fresh) — the new `rfqId` field this callable writes onto the order document must be added to all three, exactly matching `cto.md`'s own review checklist ("denylists extended for any new financial field in all three rule functions"), or a client update could rewrite an order's RFQ provenance after the fact. CLIENT WIRING DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, split to a new backlog phase RFQ-4 (mirrors RFQ-1→RFQ-2's own precedent of splitting backend-mechanism from client-UI): read `rfq_detail_screen.dart` fresh — its accepted-RFQ branch already renders `'Accepted — locked at ${finalPrice} x ${finalQuantity}'` as static text with NO purchase action at all; this phase builds and proves the callable exists and is secure, RFQ-4's job is the "Place Order" button that actually calls it. `OrderModel` (marketplace's Dart client) needs NO change: `rfqId` is server-side bookkeeping the model already tolerates being absent from, the same established pattern as `productCreditLedgerEntryId`/`commissionAmount` (confirmed: neither is modeled in `OrderModel` either, per `createOrder.ts`'s own comment). Fix: resolve each item's OWN category rate (via the same, already-read-once `categoryRates`/`resolvePayoutRate` — no new Firestore read), sum `commissionAmount = Σ(itemTotal_i × rate_i/100)` across the seller's items, then derive the stored `commissionRate` field as the resulting weighted average (`commissionAmount/grossAmount×100`) for backward-compat with anything reading that field as a single percentage — mathematically identical to, and simpler than, computing a separate weighted-rate-then-multiply step. **WS3 — D-COMMISSION-REVERSAL (N-9):** a NEW trigger, `reverseEmployeeCommissionOnCancellation`, added to `employeeCommission.ts` (co-located with `payEmployeeCommissionOnDelivery`, mirroring how `wallet.ts` already holds both `redeemReferralCode` and `completeReferralOnFirstDelivery`) — fires on the transition into a reversal-equivalent status on an order with `commissionPaid:true` and `commissionReversed` not yet `true`. Read `functions/src/customer/productCreditReversal.ts` in full as the closest existing precedent for "claw back a financial grant on order cancellation" and mirror its shape exactly: a cheap, non-authoritative pre-filter on `after` before opening a transaction; ALL reads first inside the transaction, re-deriving `employeeUid`/`commissionAmount` from the LIVE order document (never trusting `after`) as defence-in-depth against a future write path that forgets a denylist entry; idempotency re-checked AND written inside the same transaction. Deliberately uses the BROADER status set `{"cancelled","refunded","returned","rejected"}` (`confirmDelivery.ts`'s own `NOT_DELIVERABLE` set — the most complete "did not actually complete as a sale" set already established in this codebase) rather than `productCreditReversal.ts`'s narrower cancelled-only check, because D-COMMISSION-REVERSAL's own language ("cancelled/reversed") is broader than the literal string "cancelled" and this is new code with no existing narrower precedent of its own to preserve. Debits `wallets/{employeeUid}.balance` by `commissionAmount` via a plain `FieldValue.increment(-commissionAmount)` — **no floor, no insufficient-balance guard** (unlike `requestEmployeePayout.ts`'s own debit, which DOES guard — deliberately NOT mirrored here, since D-COMMISSION-REVERSAL explicitly says the balance CAN go negative). **v1 TRIGGER SAFETY (P0-FIELDVALUE precedent, applied a third time this session after FIX-8/FIX-15B):** all three files already use, or will use, the modular `import { FieldValue } from "firebase-admin/firestore"` — confirmed `employeeCommission.ts` and `sellerNotifications.ts` both already import it (from the P0-FIELDVALUE phase); the new WS3 trigger reuses that same existing import, adds none of its own. **`wallet_transactions.source` for the reversal:** reused the EXISTING `"commission"` enum value (`packages/agrimore_core/lib/models/wallet_transaction_model.dart`'s `TransactionSource`, confirmed by reading it fresh — a fixed, finite Dart enum, NOT a free-form string) with `type:"debit"` rather than inventing a new `"commission_reversal"` value, which would require a `packages/**` change (forcing a five-app analyze, out of proportion for a label) and would in any case just render as `"adjustment"` client-side on an unrecognized string (`WalletTransactionModel.fromMap`'s own `orElse: () => TransactionSource.adjustment` — confirmed by reading it, not assumed) — `source:"commission"` + `type:"debit"` is MORE informative than that fallback and needs zero `packages/**` touch. | `agrimore/fix-l1l2-surface-hardening` | `6f3f2a1` | `E2E_DEVELOP` | 2026-09-11 | session FIX-L1L2 | Phase FIX-L1L2 — close security.md tooling findings **L-1** and **L-2**, both raised against `.claude/skills/agrimore/scripts/surface.sh` and left open since FIX-2/FIX-1 (2026-09-05), re-confirmed still open by reading the current script fresh before claiming. **L-1**: when the positional `git diff --name-only "$BASE".."$HEAD"` (and its space-form fallback) both fail — e.g. a malformed invocation such as a positional path list instead of `<base> <head>` — the script currently swallows the failure: `FILES` ends up empty either way, so a genuine "diff computation failed" is printed as `LANES: none`, byte-identical to a real "no lanes, no changed files" result. A caller cannot tell the two apart, which means a security-relevant change run through a broken invocation could silently skip its lane with no error signal. **Fix**: capture the exit status of the diff attempt(s) explicitly; when both fail (and `--files` was not used), print a clear error to stderr naming the base/head that failed and exit non-zero, instead of falling through to the current unconditional `LANES: none`. Flow: mobile calls a new `createOnboardingWebHandoff` callable (mints `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`, stores `onboarding_handoffs/{code}` = `{uid, purpose:'associate_onboarding', used:false, createdAt, expiresAt: now+5min}`) → opens `${AppRoutes.baseUrl}${AppRoutes.associateOnboarding}?handoff=<code>` (`https://agrimore.in/employee/onboarding?handoff=<code>`) in the external browser via `url_launcher` (already a dependency; the SAME `launchUrl(uri, mode: LaunchMode.externalApplication)` idiom already used for payment/maps links in `checkout_screen.dart`/`payment_method_screen.dart`) → the web build's `AssociateOnboardingScreen`, on load, reads a new `handoffCode` (parsed from the route's query string by `routes.dart`, mirroring the file's own existing `/search?q=` pattern — `AssociateOnboardingScreen` is currently the ONLY branch of the routing switch that cannot carry a query string at all, since Dart's `switch` requires exact string equality against the bare `'/employee/onboarding'` constant) and calls a new `redeemOnboardingWebHandoff` callable, which — inside a single Firestore transaction (look-up + mark-`used`-atomically, so two near-simultaneous redemption attempts, e.g. a page reload firing this twice, cannot both succeed from the same still-valid code) — verifies not-yet-used and not-expired, mints `admin.auth().createCustomToken(uid)`, and returns it; the web page calls `FirebaseAuth.instance.signInWithCustomToken(...)`, and the ALREADY-REACTIVE `_EmployeeStateGate`/`AuthProvider` machinery (unchanged) resumes exactly at the payment step with no new UI to build there. TWO adjacent, pre-existing gaps in `updateCategory`'s reparent path were found while reading it for reuse, both judged in-scope because drag-and-drop makes reparenting a subtree with descendants a common, low-friction action for the first time (previously only reachable through the buried edit-dialog dropdown): (1) `updateCategory` recomputes nothing about `level` for the moved category's DESCENDANTS — the dialog's own `_saveCategory` (`category_management_screen.dart:1312`) already recomputes the moved category's OWN `level` as `resolvedParent.level + 1` before calling `updateCategory`, but neither call site has ever touched any descendant's `level`, so reparenting a category with children already silently leaves every descendant's `level` stale (wrong icon color/label) — pre-existing since CAT-3, not previously visible because the dropdown made moving a subtree rare. Fix: `updateCategory` gains a recursive descendant-`level` cascade, applied only `if isReparent`, computed as a single delta (`category.level` minus the pre-move stored level) and applied uniformly to every transitive descendant via the existing `_categoryModels`/`parentId` tree — fixes both this phase's new drag path AND the pre-existing dialog path in one place, no duplication. (2) Neither call site checks whether moving a category WITH descendants would push any of them past the model's own documented 4-level cap (`CategoryModel.level` doc: "0=Main, 1=Sub, 2=Sub-Sub, 3=Sub-Sub-Sub"; `canHaveChildren => level < 3`) — the existing `_validParentChoices()` filters candidate parents by `canHaveChildren`, which bounds the MOVED category's own new level, but never accounts for that category's own subtree height, so moving a non-leaf category onto a level-2 or level-3 parent can silently push its grandchildren past level 3 today, via the existing dialog, unnoticed because it's rare enough to not yet have been hit. Fix: a subtree-height guard (`target.level + 1 + subtreeHeight(dragged) > 3` → reject) added to this phase's own `DragTarget.onWillAcceptWithDetails`/`onAcceptWithDetails` for the new drag path specifically — NOT retrofitted onto the pre-existing dialog dropdown, which is `must_not_touch` this phase (disclosed as a found-but-deferred gap in the dialog path, not silently left unmentioned). `may_write`: `apps/admin/lib/providers/admin_provider.dart` (the `wouldCreateCategoryCycle` passthrough + `updateCategory`'s descendant-level cascade only — `_wouldCreateCategoryCycle`'s own cycle-walk logic, `addCategory`, `reorderCategory` untouched), `apps/admin/lib/screens/admin/products/category_management_screen.dart` (new Draggable/DragTarget wiring at both tree-row call sites and the header; new `_draggingCategory` state field for the header's hover hint), this ledger. `must_not_touch`: `packages/**` (no model change — `parentId`/`level` already exist), `firestore.rules`/`storage.rules`/`functions/**` (same `categories` collection, same field shapes, `allow write: if isAdmin()` re-confirmed unchanged at `firestore.rules:649-661`, no field-level validation to satisfy), CAT-5's own same-level `ReorderableListView`/`reorderCategory` mechanism, CAT-3's own edit-dialog Parent Category dropdown and its `_validParentChoices`/`_descendantsOf` (reused for cycle logic, not rewritten), any `apps/marketplace` file. Root-caused, not assumed from the report alone: the dedicated `state.sh stop <programme> <reason>` subcommand (line 52) stores `s.stop` as an object, `{ at: <iso-timestamp>, reason: <string> }` — but both rendering call sites (`show` at line 38, `status` at line 57) unconditionally read `s.stop.reason` (and `status` additionally reads `s.stop.at`), assuming that object shape without checking it. Reading a plain string's `.reason` property returns `undefined`; reading a plain string's `.at` property (without calling it) returns the inherited `String.prototype.at` method itself, whose default string coercion is exactly `function at() { [native code] }` — this explains the exact garbled text observed, not a generic "undefined" or a crash. Revalidated against CURRENT source, and WORSE than the research docs' own framing ("admin UI conflicts with rules; reject action is not allowed by that transition rule"): read `firestore.rules:2165-2190` in full — the `employee_payouts` update rule has EXACTLY ONE branch, requiring `request.resource.data.status == 'paid'`; there is NO branch permitting a transition to `'rejected'` AT ALL, so `employee_payout_detail_screen.dart`'s `_showRejectDialog` (client Firestore write, no Cloud Function involved) has ALWAYS failed with permission-denied, every single attempt. Because `requestEmployeePayout.ts` (functions/src/customer/requestEmployeePayout.ts:52-59) debits the associate's `wallets/{uid}.balance` IMMEDIATELY at request time, an admin who needs to reject a payout (e.g. bad bank details) has NO way to do so through this screen — the associate's already-debited money is stuck in limbo forever, un-recreditable via any working path. Separately, `_showMarkPaidDialog` writes `transactionRef`, but the rules' `affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` allowlist (line 2182) only contains `paymentReference` — entering a UTR reference makes the whole update fail permission-denied; leaving it blank happens to satisfy `hasOnly` and succeeds, silently steering admins toward the one path that records zero payment evidence. FIX: a new canonical callable pair, `functions/src/customer/reviewEmployeePayout.ts` (`markEmployeePayoutPaid`, `rejectEmployeePayout`), mirroring `functions/src/seller/sellerWallet.ts`'s `markWithdrawalPaidCore`/`closeWithdrawalCore` shape exactly (the closest existing sibling for "admin reviews a payout request") — idempotent via a live in-transaction status re-check, admin-claim-verified via the same `resolveIsAdmin` helper. Read `firestore.rules:228-243` in full to check whether this is a genuine security hole or a trust decision: `allow update: if isAdmin() || (isOwner(userId) && ownerCannotChangePrivilegedFields())` — the write correctly requires the caller to ALREADY be an admin (no external privilege-escalation vulnerability: a non-admin cannot reach this path, confirmed by reading the rule, not assumed), but grants that admin COMPLETELY UNRESTRICTED write access to any user's `role` field, same "admin unrestricted" shape ADMR-8 already found and left alone for `orders`. The gap, exactly like ADMR-8's, is upstream of the rules: a single admin, on a single screen, with a single tap and one "Update" press, can grant (or revoke) full Administrator access — complete platform read/write, per every `isAdmin()` check this session has read across `firestore.rules` all day — to or from ANY account, with no confirmation and no record of who did it or why. This stands out as inconsistent with this SAME admin app's own established security culture: `feature_flags_screen.dart` (`apps/admin/lib/screens/admin/benefit_program/`) already requires a mandatory reason and shows "This action is recorded in the compliance audit log" before flipping a mere feature flag — a categorically less consequential action than granting full admin access, yet the more dangerous action has strictly less friction. PROBLEM, larger than first appeared once traced fully: (1) THE FAKE BUTTON — `_buildCouponCard`'s "Apply" (line ~239) only ever ran `setState(() => _appliedCode = code)`, a purely local widget field never read by checkout, never persisted, lost the instant the screen closes — yet the button visually flips to "✓ Applied" claiming success, directly under a banner that reads "Apply coupons at checkout to save more". (2) THE SCHEMA MISMATCH, found while looking for why "Apply" wasn't wired to the real mechanism — this screen fetches raw `coupons` documents directly (`FirebaseFirestore.instance.collection('coupons').get()`) and reads field names that do **not exist** on the real, live coupon schema used everywhere else in this app (`CouponModel`/`CouponProvider`, `packages/agrimore_core/lib/models/coupon_model.dart`): reads `coupon['minOrder']` (real field: `minOrderAmount`) → always null → always shows "Min ₹0"; reads `coupon['maxUses']` (real field: `usageLimit`) → always null → always shows "X/1 used" regardless of the real limit; reads `coupon['expiry']` (real field: `validTo`) → always null/not-a-Timestamp → always shows "Expires N/A"; reads `coupon['discount']` as if pre-formatted (`'$discount OFF'`) when the real field is a plain number that needs `type` (flat/percentage/BOGO) to know whether to prefix ₹ or suffix % — so a real coupon's discount renders as a bare, unit-less number. Confirmed these are REAL, live-reachable coupons, not theoretical: `apps/admin/lib/screens/admin/coupon/coupon_management_screen.dart` (note: `screens/admin/coupon/`, NOT the `screens/admin/marketing/` directory ADMR-10 already confirmed dead and deleted — a different, live screen) is wired into `app_router.dart`, `admin_main_screen.dart`'s nav, and `admin_dashboard.dart`'s quick-actions grid ("Coupon Management — Manage offers & discounts"), and its `add_edit_coupon_dialog.dart` writes real `CouponModel.toMap()` documents via `CouponProvider.addCoupon()`. The REAL, correctly-working parallel implementation already exists and is used elsewhere in this exact app: `apps/marketplace/lib/screens/user/cart/coupon_selection_screen.dart` calls `context.read<CouponProvider>().fetchAvailableCoupons()` (which parses via `CouponModel.fromMap` and pre-filters to `.isValid` coupons only) and, on tap, `context.read<CouponProvider>().applyCoupon(coupon)` — the exact real, already-battle-tested mechanism this screen should have used from the start instead of a separate, parallel, buggy raw-Firestore path. Investigated a real risk before deciding the fix, not assumed safe: does anything re-validate `.isValid` before trusting `couponProvider.appliedCoupon` at actual checkout? `mobile_cart_screen.dart` never calls `validateCoupon()` — it trusts whatever is applied unconditionally — so a naive fix that called the bare `applyCoupon()` with an UNFILTERED (potentially expired/inactive) coupon read from this screen's own raw, unfiltered fetch would introduce a NEW money-losing bug (a customer discount-applying an expired coupon) that does not exist today, since the only currently-live entry points (`coupon_selection_screen.dart`, `blinkit_coupon_screen.dart`) both source exclusively from the pre-filtered `couponProvider.availableCoupons`. FIX (planned): replace this screen's entire data layer — drop the separate raw Firestore fetch and local `List<Map>`/`_appliedCode` state; source from `context.watch<CouponProvider>().availableCoupons` (`List<CouponModel>`, already pre-filtered to valid-only, populated via the existing, correct `fetchAvailableCoupons()`) exactly as the real, working screens already do; wire "Apply" to the real `CouponProvider.applyCoupon(coupon)` (safe here specifically because the source list is pre-filtered — the same safety property the real screens already rely on); fix every display field to the real schema (`minOrderAmount`, `usageLimit` with a 0-means-unlimited branch, `validTo`, and a new type-aware discount label — ₹X OFF / X% OFF / Buy 1 Get 1 — matching the icon/color convention already established in `blinkit_coupon_screen.dart`); reflect "✓ Applied" reactively from `couponProvider.appliedCoupon?.code`, not local widget state, so it stays correct even if the coupon was applied or removed from elsewhere in the app. Deliberately did NOT: touch `mobile_cart_screen.dart`'s own missing `validateCoupon()` call (a separate, pre-existing question about checkout's own defense-in-depth, not introduced by and out of scope for a screen-level data-binding fix); redesign this screen's visual style to match `coupon_selection_screen.dart`'s different look (kept this screen's own existing card layout/colors, changed only the data source and field mappings); touch `apps/admin/lib/screens/admin/coupon/**` (already correct, live, unrelated to this phase). may_write: `apps/marketplace/lib/screens/user/offers/offers_screen.dart`, a new or extended test under `apps/marketplace/test/`, `docs/active/BRANCH_DISPOSITIONS.md`. must_not_touch: `apps/marketplace/lib/providers/coupon_provider.dart` (already correct, not touched), `apps/marketplace/lib/screens/user/cart/{coupon_selection_screen.dart,blinkit_coupon_screen.dart,mobile_cart_screen.dart,web_cart_screen.dart}` (already correct, the models for this fix, not touched), `apps/admin/lib/screens/admin/coupon/**` (already correct, live), `packages/agrimore_core/lib/models/coupon_model.dart` (already correct schema, not touched), every other app, `firestore.rules`, `functions/**`. branch; a promotion that is not a fast-forward is refused. Pushes happen only with the owner's
word in the same message, quoted here. There is no CI and no staging Firebase project, so the
last column records the local emulator sweep and the deploy command handed to the owner — never
a deploy the skill performed.

FINDING: product variants never reached checkout — the marketplace sent only productId+quantity, orderPricing priced every line at the base product and normalizeOrderItems merged lines by productId, so a buyer who chose a differently-priced option was charged the base price (COD) or hit a payment/price mismatch (prepaid), the order recorded no option (the seller could not tell which size to ship) and variant stock never moved. Fix: items carry an optional variantId (id, or name for legacy id-less variants — the marketplace cart keeps the name); normalizeOrderItems keys by product+variant; computeOrderPricing prices and stock-checks the variant (unknown option → not-found; missing variantId = base behaviour, so older app versions keep working); order lines record variantId + variant; createOrder reads each product once and writes it once — base lines decrement stock (N-49 kept), variant lines decrement the variant inside a rewritten variants array; productCreditHold reads distinct products and its cart fingerprint includes variantId only when present (variant-free fingerprints unchanged). Clients: marketplace sends variantId on both createOrder paths; seller editor gains an Options section (name, price, stock); seller order detail shows the option. B2B stays at the product b2bPrice. | `agrimore/dlvi2-mark-all-read-semantics` | `4dd0feb` | `MERGED_DEVELOP` | 2026-09-26 | session DLVI2 (owner: "Continue in sequence"; brief §5.4, and this session's own `nav_shell_programme.md` checkpoint written during DLVI1: "confirmed real gap: `_markRead(_shown.where(...))` only marks what's currently loaded, and `unreadCount()`/`latest()` are both `.limit(kInboxSize=50)` — 'mark all' cannot cover more than the newest 50 by construction. Needs a server-side batch mark-all (or documented, honest copy) + loading/failure/race states.") | Phase DLVI2 — inbox mark-all-read semantics (workstream 5.4). PROBLEM (re-verified fresh against the just-merged DLVI1 tree, not taken on the prior checkpoint's word): `lib/inbox/rider_inbox.dart`'s `latest(riderId)` and `unreadCount(riderId)` are both `.limit(kInboxSize=50)`; `InboxScreen`'s "Mark all read" button calls `_markRead(_shown.where((n) => n.unread).map((n) => n.id))` — `_shown` is exactly the last snapshot `latest()` emitted, so it can only ever contain the newest 50 notices. A rider with more than 50 total notices (plausible over months of weekly-statement + COD + delivery-confirmation + offer notices) has older, unread notices that are structurally invisible to this screen (no load-more/pagination exists here, unlike `RiderHistoryScreen`'s own cursor pattern) and therefore can never be reached or cleared by "Mark all read", no matter how many times it is tapped — the unread badge (correctly capped at showing "50+" via `unreadBadgeText`, not lying) would perpetually show a non-zero count the button can never actually clear to zero. Independently verified this is fixable client-side, not a rules/backend gap: `firestore.rules:285-293`'s `notifications/{notificationId}` rule already grants the owner `read` (no query-shape restriction — Firestore rules gate per-document access, not query cardinality, so an UNBOUNDED `.where('unread', isEqualTo: true)` query needs no rule change) and `update` restricted to exactly `['unread','read','readAt']` (the same shape `markRead`'s existing batches already write); `firestore.indexes.json:129-142` already carries a composite index on `(unread ASC, createdAt DESC)` and `fieldOverrides` is empty (line 840), so `unread`'s automatic single-field index is active and a plain equality filter needs no new index. Opened the directly-relevant mockup fresh (`30-delivery-history-inbox/06-unread-mark-all-read.png`, "30.6 Unread states & mark all as read") before scoping: confirms mark-all "updates only the read status, never deletes inbox items" (matches `markRead`'s existing shape) and "individual items are marked as read when opened and confirmed" (matches `_open()`'s existing per-item `_markRead([n.id])`); also depicts a disabled/loading button state while in flight ("Marking as read..."), a success toast ("All notifications marked as read") shown only after server confirmation, and a distinct failure state ("Couldn't mark notifications as read") — none of the loading/success/failure feedback exists in the current button today (bare `TextButton` with no busy state, and failure already shows a toast via `inboxMarkReadFailed` but there is no success toast at all, and nothing disables the button against duplicate taps). SCOPE: `RiderInboxSource` gains `markAllRead(riderId)` — queries `.where('unread', isEqualTo: true)` with NO `.limit()` (deliberately unbounded, unlike `latest()`/`unreadCount()`, since this must reach every unread notice regardless of how many exist), batches the SAME `{unread:false, read:true, readAt:serverTimestamp()}` update in groups of 400 exactly like `markRead`'s existing loop (extracted/shared, not duplicated). `InboxScreen`'s "Mark all read" button becomes a small stateful control: disabled + shows a progress indicator while an in-flight call exists (a `bool _markingAll` field, guarding against duplicate taps the mockup itself calls out); on success shows a new success toast (new ARB key); on failure reuses the existing `inboxMarkReadFailed` toast, button re-enabled either way. may_write: `apps/delivery/lib/inbox/rider_inbox.dart`, `apps/delivery/lib/screens/inbox/inbox_screen.dart`, `apps/delivery/lib/l10n/app_en.arb` + generated localization files, `apps/delivery/test/**`, `apps/delivery/integration_test/screens_tour_test.dart`, this ledger row, `~/.agrimore/run/delivery-ui-redesign/**`. must_not_touch: `firestore.rules`, `firestore.indexes.json` (deliberately — both already support this fix with zero changes, confirmed above, not assumed), every other app, `packages/**`, `functions/**`. Explicitly NOT in scope this phase, recorded rather than silently chased: the mockup's own All/Unread filter tabs, Today/Earlier time-grouping, per-type icons and a dot-based unread indicator (these appeared across BOTH the 05 and 06 mockups during DLVI1's own review and are a general inbox-visual-redesign concern spanning multiple workstreams, not specific to mark-all-read semantics); a persistent error banner with an inline Retry action instead of a toast for the failure case (the mockup's own Panel 4) — the same toast-vs-persistent-card tension already found and deliberately deferred in DLVH3 (statement-unavailable) and DLVI1 (delivery-unavailable/network-error), now a THIRD confirmed instance, arguably deserving its own dedicated pass per the brief's own instruction not to spend the whole assignment polishing feedback surfaces piecemeal. Collision check 2026-09-26: `git worktree list` (`Agrimore-sredesign` only, on `agrimore/sredesign1-seller-ui` — a different app, zero overlap); `git branch --list 'agrimore/*'` (every other branch already `MERGED_DEVELOP`); no other `ACTIVE` row in this ledger — built in an isolated `../Agrimore-dlvi2` worktree branched from `develop` @ `056f426` (DLVI1's own merge + both bookkeeping commits). (a Refresh-assignment loading state, with a grayed-out placeholder list AND the safety-reminder card already visible even while checking), "Delivery details changed" (a dismissible banner on top of the SAME already-current order summary/customer/items/payment/earnings, with a "Review changes" action), "This delivery is no longer assigned to you" (a full block: icon, title, "The assignment has been changed. You can't view the delivery details for privacy.", "Back to dashboard" + "Contact support" buttons), "Couldn't confirm your assignment" (a Retry button, "Last known: At pickup", a compact last-known summary card -- Merchant shown in full, Customer masked, Items/Payment shown as summary only -- and "Delivery actions unavailable"); a state-flow diagram (Refresh assignment -> Still assigned/resume latest step | Changed/review latest info | Removed/clear private details); a "Key points" list whose masking instruction is scoped ONLY to the connection-lost case ("If connection is lost, show last known step, mask customer details and disable delivery actions" -- no masking instruction appears against the "changed" bullet, which just says "show a clear message and ask the driver to review"); and a "Safety reminder" card ("Already carrying the order? Fixed by making each `activeSource` a small `async*` function that synthesizes the "present" baseline directly at subscribe time, then continues from the controller -- guaranteed delivered regardless of subscribe timing. ADMR-4 fixed the EXACT SAME root bug -- a low-stock check that reads only a product's BASE `stock` field, invisible to any product whose stock lives in `variants[].stock` (every variant-line sale decrements a variant's own stock, per `createOrder.ts`, never the base field) -- in TWO locations: the backend trigger (`onProductStockChanged`) and the seller app's own `isLowStock()` (`apps/seller/lib/providers/seller_product_provider.dart`). PROBLEM, re-investigated fresh against current merged source: `functions/src/customer/restoreStockOnCancellation.ts` (a generic Firestore trigger on ANY transition into `cancelled`, regardless of which caller wrote it) auto-restores stock unconditionally, including when the PRIOR status was `delivered` -- confirmed by reading its transition guard directly (`wasCancelled`/`isNowCancelled` only, no check of what `before` actually was). `adminOrderActions.ts`'s own `checkOrderTransitionAllowed` is the only currently-reachable path into this transition (`sellerTransitionOrder.ts`'s own `cancel` action only allows `from: ['confirmed','processing']`, confirmed by reading its `TRANSITIONS` table directly -- never `delivered`); the fix lives in the trigger, not the caller, so it is correct regardless of which caller reaches this transition, matching the trigger's own established "closes the last path, uniformly" design. A delivered order means the customer already has physical possession -- auto-restoring stock the instant admin flips the status to cancelled claims a unit is sellable again before anyone has confirmed it physically came back, a real double-commit-inventory risk, not a hypothetical one. The mega-prompt's own explicit boundary: do not invent return/refund/inspection POLICY (none exists anywhere in this codebase today), keep the dependent intervention read-only/unavailable where undecided, do not silently choose financial/inventory liability policy. SCOPE, deliberately the narrowest fix that closes the real gap without deciding anything undecided: (1) `restoreStockOnCancellation.ts`'s per-item restoration logic extracted verbatim into an exported `restoreOrderItemStock(tx, db, order, orderId)` -- zero logic change, pure extraction, so the automatic and manual paths can never drift apart on HOW a unit is restored, only WHEN. (2) The trigger gains one new branch: if `before` was `delivered`, do not restore -- instead `set({stockRestorePending:true}, {merge:true})` and return (a plain idempotent flag merge, not a transaction; does not recurse the same trigger, since the recursive event's own `before` already shows `cancelled`, caught by the existing `wasCancelled` guard). Every other transition into `cancelled` (the overwhelming majority -- pre-delivery, no physical handoff yet) is completely unaffected. (3) New admin-only callable `functions/src/admin/confirmOrderReturnReceived.ts` -- the SOLE path that resolves a pending flag, by calling the SAME extracted `restoreOrderItemStock`, then setting `stockRestored:true`, `stockRestorePending:false`, `stockRestoreConfirmedBy/At`. Deliberately takes NO inspection/condition/quantity data (a binary "items are back, restore them" action) -- refund timing, restocking fees and partial-quantity returns all stay genuinely open, not silently resolved here. Idempotent via the same in-transaction re-check style `restoreStockOnCancellation.ts` itself already established (re-check `stockRestored`/`stockRestorePending` live inside the transaction), not a new requestId idiom, since this is a one-shot admin confirmation, not a retry-prone client action. (4) `OrderModel` gains `stockRestored`/`stockRestorePending` (5-location pattern: declaration/constructor/fromMap/toMap/copyWith) and `OrderProvider` gains `confirmOrderReturnReceived(orderId)` (deliberately does NOT touch the shared `isLoading`/`error` state `updateOrderStatus` uses, since a single confirm tap swapping the WHOLE screen to its loading view would hide the very button just pressed -- mirrors this screen's own existing local-busy-flag convention, `_loadingInvoice`/`_exportInvoice`, instead). (5) `admin_order_details_screen.dart`'s existing Cancellation card gains, only when `order.deliveredAt != null`: two new pure top-level predicates (`orderNeedsReturnConfirmation`, `orderShowsStockRestoredNote`, mirroring ADMR-36's own `codLiabilityLabel` extraction so the decision is directly testable without constructing this screen -- confirmed still impossible outside a real Firebase app per `order_360_layout_test.dart`'s own header) gating an honest orange prompt + a "Confirm Return Received" button (local `_confirmingReturn` busy flag, disabled while in flight) when a return confirmation is genuinely still needed, or a small neutral note when stock has already been restored; PROBLEM, re-investigated fresh against current merged source: `OrderProvider.updateOrderStatus` (`apps/admin/lib/providers/order_provider.dart`) generates `const Uuid().v4()` fresh on EVERY call -- confirmed by reading the method directly, no state carried between calls. `adminUpdateOrderStatus`'s own server-side idempotency (an `orders/{orderId}/adminActions/{requestId}` doc, checked/written inside the transaction) exists SPECIFICALLY to make a retried call safe -- but since the client never reuses a requestId, a genuine retry after an AMBIGUOUS failure (a dropped connection or timeout where the first call may have already committed server-side) always mints a brand-new id, so the server's own replay-detection can never fire for the one case it exists to protect: the retry looks like a completely unrelated fresh action to the server, and could apply the SAME mutating transition twice (double-firing a refund-status stamp, a duplicate timeline entry, etc.) Separately, confirmed the server's existing idempotency check itself has a real, narrower gap of its own: when `actionSnap.exists`, it returns the CACHED prior outcome unconditionally, with NO check that the CURRENT call's `newStatus`/`reason` actually matches what was originally recorded under that requestId -- a requestId reused (by a client bug, or a genuinely different action mistakenly reusing an old id) with DIFFERENT parameters would silently get back a stale, mismatched result instead of a clear refusal. SCOPE: (1) client -- `PendingStatusUpdate` (a plain, Firebase-free class: orderId/newStatus/description/requestId + a `matches` check) and a single `OrderProvider._pendingStatusUpdate` field track the one action whose outcome is still unknown; `updateOrderStatus` reuses that pending requestId ONLY when the new call is an identical retry (same order/status/reason), otherwise mints a fresh one. The pending state is deliberately NOT cleared on success — it is cleared to null there — nor on a DEFINITE server rejection (`isAmbiguousFunctionsErrorCode` distinguishes transport/availability codes -- `unavailable`/`deadline-exceeded`/`internal`/`cancelled`/`unknown` -- where the outcome is genuinely unknown, from definite ones like `permission-denied`/`invalid-argument` where the server demonstrably applied nothing); it is also deliberately NOT reset by `clearSelectedOrder`/`dispose`, since a retry must survive the admin navigating away and back. Both `PendingStatusUpdate` and `isAmbiguousFunctionsErrorCode` are public (not underscore-prefixed) specifically for direct testability, mirroring ADMR-36/37's own `codLiabilityLabel`/`orderNeedsReturnConfirmation` extraction pattern, given `OrderProvider` itself cannot be constructed outside a real Firebase app. (2) server -- `adminOrderActions.ts`'s existing-action branch now compares `prior.toStatus`/`prior.reason` against the current call's `newStatus`/`reason` and returns `validation_failed` (\"already used for a different action\") on any mismatch, instead of silently replaying a stale cached result. may_write: `apps/admin/lib/providers/order_provider.dart`, `apps/admin/test/order_status_update_idempotency_test.dart` (new), `functions/src/admin/adminOrderActions.ts`, `functions/scripts/phase64_admin_order_status_command_test.js`, this ledger row, `~/.agrimore/run/agrimore-admin-restructure/**`. must_not_touch: `confirmOrderReturnReceived.ts` (ADMR-37's own callable already correct on its own established idempotency style for a one-shot admin confirmation -- re-checking `stockRestored`/`stockRestorePending` live inside its transaction -- and does not need a requestId/retry mechanism of this kind at all), `checkOrderTransitionAllowed`/`isDangerousOrderStatusTransition` (unrelated, unchanged), every other admin card/provider, every other app. Deploy consequence: `firebase deploy --only functions:adminUpdateOrderStatus` (the mismatch-rejection is new server behavior). PROBLEM, re-investigated fresh against current merged source: `OrderProvider.loadOrderById` (confirmed by reading it directly) never reset `_selectedOrder`/any of its nine subrecords before starting a new load -- an order-not-found result, an error, or simply the load still being in flight all left a PREVIOUS order's data sitting in shared state under a DIFFERENT order's id. Separately, and more seriously: all nine sub-loaders (`_loadOrderTimeline`/`_loadDispatchOffers`/`_loadRiderEarning`/`_loadCommissionExceptions`/`_loadRelatedSupportTickets`/`_loadDeliveryExceptions`/`_loadRiderIncidents`/`_loadSellerPayouts`/`_loadRiderCashAccount`) are plain `await`ed Firestore reads with NO guard at all against a second `loadOrderById` call starting before the first one finishes -- confirmed by reading every one directly: none checks any kind of call-identity before writing its result. Concretely: navigating from order A's detail screen to order B's (or a single screen re-fetching after two rapid actions) can let order A's slower response land AFTER order B's faster one, silently overwriting the correct, currently-displayed order B data with stale order A data -- a classic out-of-order-completion race, not a hypothetical one, since Firestore latency genuinely varies per call. SCOPE, the complete fix, not a partial mitigation: (1) a monotonic `_orderLoadGeneration` counter, bumped by `loadOrderById` (returning the NEW value it captures as its own `generation`), by `clearSelectedOrder()`, and by `dispose()`. (2) `loadOrderById` resets all ten selected-order fields (the order itself + nine subrecords) to null/empty IMMEDIATELY, before any await -- not only on a successful fetch -- so a not-found/error/still-in-flight state never shows a previous order's data. (3) EVERY ONE of the nine sub-loaders now takes the `generation` it was called with as an explicit second parameter and, the instant its own single await resolves -- before writing anything, including its own `_isLoadingXxx`/error flags -- checks `if (generation != _orderLoadGeneration) return;`; an older, superseded call's response is discarded silently rather than landing on top of newer data. `loadOrderById` itself carries the identical guard at three points: right after its own order-document fetch, right after the full sub-loader chain completes, and in its own catch block. Verified by direct count: 22 real occurrences of the exact guard condition across all ten methods (`loadOrderById` -- 3; eight of the nine sub-loaders -- 2 each; `_loadRiderCashAccount` -- 3, its own extra early-return branch for a null/empty riderId also guarded). No sub-loader's own query or parsing logic was touched -- this is purely an orchestration-safety change layered on top of unchanged reads. may_write: `apps/admin/lib/providers/order_provider.dart`, this ledger row, `~/.agrimore/run/agrimore-admin-restructure/**`. must_not_touch: every sub-loader's own Firestore query/parsing (unchanged, verified by diff), `admin_order_details_screen.dart` (its two `loadOrderById(widget.orderId)` call sites need no change -- the public signature is unchanged, only internal orchestration), every other provider, every other app. Deploy consequence: NONE -- purely a client-side race-safety fix; ships in the admin app's next build with no `firebase deploy` at all. PROBLEM, confirmed by direct read of `registration_draft.dart` and `rider_registration_screen.dart` before any code was written: `_draftKey => _service.backend.currentUid ?? '_pending'` is correct on its own, but `_loadResumableDraft()` reads `final own = await _draftStore.load(key); if (own != null) return own; if (key == '_pending') return null; return _draftStore.load('_pending');` -- an UNCONDITIONAL fallback to the shared pre-account slot whenever a SIGNED-IN rider (any uid) has no draft of their own yet, with no check that this signed-in rider is the same person who created that pending draft. Concretely: rider A abandons registration before an account exists (draft saved under the shared `_pending` key, the only slot available pre-account); later, a DIFFERENT, already-registered rider B signs in on the same device and for any reason reaches `RiderRegistrationScreen` with `initial == null` (a fresh registration path, not a resubmission, which instead resumes from the server's own authoritative record and never calls `_checkForDraft` at all) -- B's own key lookup misses, and the fallback silently hands B rider A's own name/phone/address/aadhaar/bank details as an offered "resume" prompt. The existing file-header comment claiming "so a signed-in rider's draft never leaks to a different account" was itself wrong -- the fallback is exactly what allows the leak; corrected as part of this phase. The fallback's own stated justification (a crash between `ensureAccount()` succeeding inside `submitAll()` and the next incidental `_saveDraft()` call, which only happens at a step-advance or photo-pick, not at account creation itself) is a real, separate need -- addressed here by ELIMINATING the gap it was compensating for, not by keeping the unsafe compensation. SCOPE: (1) `_submit()` now calls `_service.ensureAccount(_form)` explicitly BEFORE `submitAll()` (idempotent -- `ensureAccount` already returns the existing uid immediately once one exists, confirmed by reading `rider_application.dart`'s own doc comment and body; calling it twice is the same call `submitAll` already made internally, not new Firebase traffic beyond what already happened) and immediately re-saves the draft under the now-current key -- so any crash from that point through the entire upload/submit sequence leaves the draft already correctly owned by the new account, never needing a cross-key fallback. (2) `_loadResumableDraft()` reduced to `_draftStore.load(_draftKey)` -- no fallback, ever; a signed-in rider only ever sees a draft filed under their own uid. (3) An age check (`isDraftExpired`, `registrationDraftMaxAge = Duration(days: 14)`, both pure top-level functions/constants, directly unit-testable): a draft older than this is silently cleared rather than ever offered, closing "abandoned drafts have a defined retention/cleanup path" without inventing a server-side mechanism for what is still purely on-device state. (4) `_clearDraft()` (already called on both successful submission and explicit discard) now also best-effort-deletes the actual staged photo-cache files a draft's `DraftPhoto.path` values point at, not just the secure-storage JSON entry -- closing "discard removes the appropriate stored values and staged files" (previously only the metadata was cleared; the picked-image cache copies, including Aadhaar/selfie photos, were left on disk indefinitely). (5) `WidgetsBindingObserver` added (mirroring the exact precedent already established by `device_readiness_screen.dart`, DLVOA1) so `didChangeAppLifecycleState(paused/inactive)` proactively saves the current step's in-progress edits -- closing the brief's own separately-named "current-step edits... lost when leaving or terminating the app" gap, without per-keystroke writes (still only on step-advance, photo-pick, pre-submit and now backgrounding -- a bounded set of real save points, not continuous). Verified by tracing rather than assumed safe, and recorded here explicitly rather than left silent: "late reads/writes from a previous session cannot repopulate the new session's form" is ALREADY structurally true and required no additional fix -- `_draftKey` is captured into a local synchronously, before any `await`, at the moment each save/load is invoked (Dart evaluates everything before a function's first `await` synchronously at the call site), so a slow-completing secure-storage write always lands under the key that was correct when it was triggered, never one a later, unrelated sign-in changed the global `FirebaseAuth.instance.currentUser` to in the meantime; and each screen instance's own `_form`/`_photos`/`mounted`/`_draftChecked` fields are private to that State object, so a disposed instance's late-completing `_checkForDraft()` cannot write into a different, newer instance's fields even in principle. may_write: `apps/delivery/lib/screens/auth/rider_registration_screen.dart`, `apps/delivery/lib/registration/registration_draft.dart` (header comment only), `apps/delivery/test/**`, this ledger row, `~/.agrimore/run/delivery-ui-redesign/**`. must_not_touch: `rider_application.dart`/`RegistrationService`/`RegistrationBackend` (already correct and idempotent, read for reuse, not modified), `registration_draft_test.dart`'s own existing JSON-level coverage (old-schema/corrupt-data handling already correct, not touched), every other app. Deploy consequence: NONE (client-only; no backend/rules/schema change -- the draft remains purely on-device). Existing on-device drafts: not migrated (no JSON schema change), but behaviorally, a device that currently has a stray `_pending` draft AND a signed-in rider with no draft of their own will, after this phase ships, no longer auto-offer that stale draft -- a one-time, disclosed, deliberate trade-off (the rider re-enters their in-progress form once) in exchange for closing a real cross-account privacy leak; no data is deleted by the change itself. | `agrimore/dlvbank1-exact-request-routing` | `3d21b86e` | `MERGED_DEVELOP` | 2026-09-27 | owner (2026-09-27 final-closure programme brief, section 5: "First implementation: exact bank-change-request routing") | Phase DLVBANK1 -- the owner's own explicit first-priority item for the final-closure programme, directly building on this session's own prior finding (recorded in `~/.agrimore/run/delivery-ui-redesign/state.json`'s `bank_change_notice_routing_investigated_2026-09-27` key): a bank-change approval/rejection notification currently opens a GENERIC destination (the Earnings tab, via `NoticeTarget.payoutDetails`) rather than the SPECIFIC request it concerns, because `bankReviewNotice()` (`riderNotices.ts`) never wrote the request's own id into the notice's `data` map in the first place -- unlike `identityChangeNotice()`/`documentReviewNotice()`/`supportRequestNotice()`, which all already carry their own specific id (`requestId`/`submissionId`/`ticketId`). DLVID3 already solved this EXACT problem for identity-change requests (2026-09-27, merged `f8627e7e`): server writes `requestId`, client's `RiderNotice.fromMap` already parses `data['requestId']` GENERICALLY (not gated to any one type), and a dedicated `IdentityChangeScreen(requestId:)` mode resolves and pins to that one historical request via `RiderIdentityBackend.requestById(requestId)` -- a direct client Firestore doc read gated entirely by the security rule's own owner-or-admin ownership check, never a callable. Confirmed fresh (not assumed from the precedent alone): `firestore.rules`'s own `rider_bank_change_requests` block (line 2149) already carries the IDENTICAL rule shape as `rider_identity_change_requests` (line 2157) -- an owner-or-admin read, the same `resource.data.riderId` ownership check either collection already uses -- so a per-id owner read of a SPECIFIC bank-change request is already fully authorized today, zero rules change needed. SCOPE, mirroring the identity precedent file-for-file: (1) `bankReviewNotice(requestId, approved, reason)` -- both branches' `data` map gains `requestId` (currently `{ type: '...' }` only) -- a 2-line backend change, no schema change (the field the notice needs to carry already exists as the function's own first parameter, just never written into `data`). (2) `RiderMoneyService` gains `bankChangeRequestById(String requestId)`, a `Stream.multi`-wrapped direct doc read on `rider_bank_change_requests/{requestId}`, mirroring `RiderIdentityBackend.requestById` structurally (same deferred-touch pattern, same null-for-missing-or-not-mine semantics enforced by the rule itself, not app code, matching the exact ownership check that collection's own rule already applies). (3) `NoticeTarget` gains `bankChangeRequest`; the `target` getter's `bank_change_approved`/`bank_change_rejected` case becomes `requestId != null ? NoticeTarget.bankChangeRequest : NoticeTarget.payoutDetails` -- an OLD notice written before this fix (no `requestId` in its `data`) keeps the EXISTING generic Earnings-tab behavior unchanged (an honest fallback to what already worked, never a regression to "nothing happens" the way DLVID3's OWN identity fallback chose (`NoticeTarget.none`) -- bank-change's fallback is deliberately more forgiving since the pre-existing behavior was never broken, just imprecise). (4) new `BankChangeRequestScreen` (own file, mirroring `IdentityChangeScreen`'s exact state shape): loading (`ConnectionState.waiting`) / not-found (deleted or not this rider's, enforced by the rule) / approved / pending / rejected-with-a-"Correct and resend" action. Reuses this session's own EXISTING `_PayoutDetails` copy (`l.bankChangeReviewing`/`l.bankChangeRejected(reason)`/`l.bankChangeRejectedNoReason`, already shipped) for the pending/rejected bodies -- only an "approved" title/body and a "not found" title/body are genuinely new copy, since the current inline widget never had an approved-specific message (an approved request just silently becomes the new active payout details). (5) `MoneyScreen`'s own private `_BankChangeForm` renamed to public `BankChangeForm` (zero behavior change, purely so `BankChangeRequestScreen`'s own "Correct and resend" can reopen the SAME real form rather than duplicating one) -- deliberately does NOT pre-fill the rejected request's own raw account number/IFSC into the reopened form (unlike identity's own name/vehicle pre-fill): those raw values are sensitive banking details this app already takes care to mask everywhere else in the UI, and pre-filling them back into an editable field would be a new, elevated exposure surface for a “correct and resend” convenience DLVID3's own precedent didn't have to weigh (a plain, unmasked NAME is not the same class of sensitive value as an account number); the rejected request's own MASKED account/UPI are shown as read-only reference text instead, and the rider re-enters fresh, exactly as a first-time request would. (6) `inbox_screen.dart` gains `_openBankChangeRequest(RiderNotice n)`, mirroring `_openIdentityRequest` exactly, wired into the `_open()` switch's new `NoticeTarget.bankChangeRequest` case. Today's four call sites (Customer/Seller/Delivery/Associate 360) all key each list by entity id, so Flutter's own key-based element reconciliation happens to dodge this by creating a fresh State per entity -- but the component itself is not defensively correct, and the very next planned caller (a filterable case queue) would hit it directly. (B) CONFIRMED -- the initial-failure branch (_error != null && _docs.isEmpty) renders SectionMessage with no button at all; an admin who hits a transient error on first load has no in-UI way to retry without leaving and reopening the screen. The later-page-failure branch already has an implicit retry (the Load More button reappears, since _hasMore is never cleared on error) -- only the initial state lacks one. (C) CONFIRMED -- rider_detail_screen.dart's _EarningsTab (line ~534) does .where(riderId==).limit(300).get() with NO orderBy, then sorts the fetched page client-side. Because there is no server-side ordering, Firestore returns an UNDEFINED subset of up to 300 matching documents for a rider with more than 300 -- the client sort only orders WHATEVER CAME BACK, which is not guaranteed to be the 300 most recent; a genuinely recent delivery could be silently absent while an old one appears. (D) CONFIRMED, same defect, three more sites: rider_detail_screen.dart's _RiderScopedList (used for rider_support_tickets, rider_incidents and delivery_exceptions, limit 100 each) and associate_detail_screen.dart's _CommissionTab (commission_exceptions, limit 100) -- all equality-only + limit + client-sort, all with the identical undefined-subset defect. All five were built this way in ADMR-58/59 specifically to AVOID a missing composite index, mirroring rider_payouts_screen.dart's own pre-existing _StatementsTab convention (which has the same latent defect, out of scope here since it is a must_not_touch global queue, not part of this phase) -- the owner's own prompt correctly identifies this as the wrong tradeoff: avoiding an index deploy is not sufficient justification for a query that cannot guarantee it shows genuinely recent records. SCOPE: (1) PaginatedQueryList gains an optional resetKey parameter (any Object?, compared by value not identity of the Query itself, since Query objects have no stable equality and comparing them would risk a reset loop on every rebuild) -- when resetKey changes between didUpdateWidget calls, all loaded state clears and a fresh fetch begins, invalidating any in-flight request tied to the old query via the existing _requestId guard; today's four callers are UNCHANGED (they pass no resetKey, preserving their existing correct-by-keying behavior) -- this is additive, not a breaking change to any of them. (2) The initial-failure state gains a real 'Try again' button calling the existing _loadMore(), which already works correctly once re-invoked (the existing _hasMore/_loading guards are unaffected by this addition). (3) All five equality+limit+client-sort sites are rewritten to use PaginatedQueryList itself with real server-side .orderBy(createdAt, descending: true), giving genuine, complete-in-order pagination identical in correctness to the four People-360 workspaces' own Orders/Catalog/Assignments/Attribution tabs -- requiring five new composite indexes this phase adds to firestore.indexes.json: rider_earnings(riderId ASC, createdAt DESC), rider_support_tickets(riderId ASC, createdAt DESC), rider_incidents(riderId ASC, createdAt DESC), delivery_exceptions(riderId ASC, createdAt DESC), commission_exceptions(employeeUid ASC, createdAt DESC) -- confirmed none of these five already exist by reading firestore.indexes.json in full before scoping.
